podcast.title: Renowned Producer for Bedi (2010)
podcast.body: Described as "one of the most important and expensive producers in the United Kingdom," Steve Lily Wipe is known for having worked with prominent bands like U2. Liam Gallagher hired him at "a fortune" to produce Bedi's debut album, aiming for a grand musical comeback. "Steve Lily Wipe que es uno de los productores más importantes y más caros del reino unido que ha trabajado con gente como youtube, en el que se gasta una auténtica millonada para hacer un poco una vuelta por todo lo alto."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Diverse Production Credits
podcast.body: Lillywhite's production portfolio includes collaborations with a wide range of artists, such as Morrissey, The Pogues, Simple Minds, Talking Heads, Dave Matthews, and Chris Cornell. "He's also worked with Morrissey and The Pogues and Simple Mines and Talking Heds and Dave Matthews and Chris Cornell and tons of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Work with U2
podcast.body: He has notably produced approximately half of all the albums released by U2. "He worked on about half of all the albums you two has ever done."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Marriage to Kirsty MacColl
podcast.body: He was previously married to the English singer-songwriter Kirsty MacColl and produced some of her records. "Steve used to be married to an English singer-songwriter named Kristi McCall. A couple of her records were produced by Steve."

xref.title: Band Without a Drummer
xref.body: The Sam Willows are noted for not having a proper drummer. Their song "Glass House" was originally described as a "Mumford and Son's Fokie thing" before Steve Lillywhite's production transformed it. "The song originally was a nice, well, Mumford and Son's Fokie thing without a proper drummer. In fact, the band doesn't have a drummer."

xref.title: Steve Lillywhite Production Week in Singapore
xref.body: The Sam Willows, a band from Singapore, worked with British producer Steve Lillywhite for a week in a local studio as part of a project initiated by the local Music Industry Association. They put in "four 12-hour days" recording one of their songs, with Lillywhite later mixing the tracks in his LA studio. "The group is called the Sam Willows, and they put in four 12-hour days in a studio, and then Steve took the tracks back with him to LA to mix it in his own studio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Steve Lillywhite's Role
xref.body: Producer Steve Lillywhite, known for his work on U2's first three albums, played a crucial role in the development of "Fairy Tale of New York." He produced The Pogues' third album, "If I Should Fall From Grace With God," and, being married to Kirsty MacColl, arranged for her to record the female vocal parts. "The producer was a guy named Steve Lillie White. He had helped you too with their first three albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
